evidence.text: Supply-chain and analyst evidence that December-quarter iPhone 18 Pro volumes are being cut: Nikkei Asia (2026-10-09) reported October component orders for 18 Pro/Pro Max cut at least 15-20% from Apple's original request; Loop Capital (2026-10-20, downgrade to Hold, PT $330) models 79M December-quarter iPhones vs ~85M Street and ASP $1,123 vs $1,239, citing a 13M-unit second-half cut it no longer expects recovered; Jefferies (2026-10-19) says China Pro lead times have fallen to zero with 10-15% component cuts. evidence.text: The reported quarter should land at or slightly above the $27.5m bar. Q1 FY27 opened with $80.6m of contracted backlog, all of it scheduled to ship within 12 months under the 10-K definition. On 2026-07-14 the CEO said Sonoma package-level shipments start 'during this quarter' with the bulk in Q2. The CFO said H1 is likely the same as or better than H2: on the $130-150m guide that is $65-75m+ for H1, of which consensus puts only $27.5m in Q1. The company has beaten EPS in 3 of the last 4 quarters and matched once; Q4 FY26 printed $18.8m against $17.92m consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-07-14) beat revenue, $18.8m vs $17.92m, and set a record for bookings; the stock rose +21.9%, but the move was driven by the first FY27 guide. Q3 FY26 (2026-04-07) +25.7% came with a record $41m order. The 2025-10-06 and 2025-07-08 prints (-17.4%, -12.4%) turned on guidance withdrawal and order timing, not the reported quarter. These are confirmed 8-K 2.02 releases; the fiscal-year change relabels the quarters but does not make them non-events.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved in 30 days (Zacks ESP 0.00%), so estimates did not react to the CFO's 'first half same or better' remark. The ~$27.5m is roughly 20% of the guide midpoint, which is conservative if H1 is half of the year. If the market expected a large Q1 beat, revisions would have risen and the skew would not be put-heavy. Q1 sits inside the guided year, so a beat mainly confirms the guide; size kept small.
evidence.independence: The backlog definition comes from a different document, the FY2026 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040470/000165495426006919/aehr_10k.htm). The cadence comment comes from the call transcript only.

evidence.text: Q1 bookings are at least partly visible: a $22m follow-on wafer-level AI processor order on 2026-08-12, plus a silicon photonics follow-on on 2026-08-04 (amount undisclosed, shipping H1 CY2027). Both fall inside the 06-27 to 09-25 quarter and come on top of the $100.6m effective backlog, which already counted bookings through the first two weeks of FY27. A further ~$6m hyperscaler order arrived on 2026-10-07, after quarter end. Announced orders since the guide therefore lift visibility to roughly $128m+ against a $130-150m year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings have been the line this stock trades on: the record $60.7m bookings quarter (2026-07-14) rose +21.9%; the $41m order quarter (2026-04-07) rose +25.7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Each order was press-released and is public, so book-to-bill near or above 1 is largely known. What is not public is the unannounced bookings total (Aehr does not release every order) and the ending backlog. Had the market priced strong bookings, the stock would not have fallen 49% in the month the orders accumulated, though that fall is mostly sector-driven (see positioning finding).
evidence.independence: Separate PRs: https://www.aehr.com/2026/08/aehr-test-systems-expands-silicon-photonics-production-momentum-with-follow-on-production-order-from-lead-customer/ and https://www.webull.com/news/15706757494473728 (2026-10-07). Shares the backlog base with finding 1.

evidence.text: The lead hyperscaler's second, higher-power AI device has slipped. The April 2026 PR said it was 'expected to move to production later this year'; on the July call it was 'delayed but still expected to start ramping this fiscal year'; the 2026-10-07 PR says 'expected production ramp ... in calendar 2027'. The third device is 'not even this fiscal year'. The slip puts part of the FY27 Sonoma revenue the guide relies on (the CEO put package-level revenue at 'probably $50 million') into H2 FY27 or beyond, which threatens the top of the $130-150m range or a raise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-07-08 print (-12.4%) and 2025-10-06 print (-17.4%) were guidance-withholding or order-delay prints; per itiger, 'Aehr's Stock Slides After Withholding Guidance, Order Delays'. On this name, delay language on the guide has cost double digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: The timing wording moved from 'later this year' (April) to 'calendar 2027' (October) in a press release whose headline was an order. No preview cited the slip; consensus FY numbers are unchanged. Had it been priced, sell-side revisions to FY27 would show, and none appear. Calendar 2027 still sits inside FY27 (ends 2027-06-25), so the guide can hold; that, the crowded short and the ~17% short float shrink the size.
evidence.independence: The July call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15228507339449344) independently records the delay. The April PR (https://www.aehr.com/2026/04/aehr-receives-record-41-million-production-order-from-lead-hyperscale-ai-customer-second-half-bookings-exceed-92-million/) gives the original timing.

evidence.text: Part of the October drawdown was attributed to Teradyne's 2026-10-06 launch of Titan HP with burn-in capability; AEHR fell about 11.7% that day to about $92 from $107 on 10-02. evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is pricing some competitive threat; Titan HP is package-level and system-level test with a burn-in feature, while Aehr's growth engines are wafer-level FOX-XP and package-level Sonoma. If the market saw no threat, AEHR would not have underperformed SOX (-15.7% Oct 6-16) by about 3x. A rebuttal is inference about the call, so the size is small and runs against the +11.75 skew.

evidence.text: Skilling is decelerating against the company's own full-year claim. In May the company said it expected 'double-digit Skilling revenue growth for the full year' with acceleration as the year went on. Instead Skilling grew +9% y/y in Q1 ($17.6M) and +2% in Q2 ($17.5M), and the Q2 release dropped the separate Skilling guide in favour of total revenue only. Full-year double-digit growth now needs high-teens growth in H2, so a walk-back or a miss on the growth narrative is likely at this print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moved this name on its last prints: -14.56% (Aug 2026, Q3 guide cut), -10.67% (Feb 2026), -31.41% (Feb 2025). No print in the baseline shows a separate reaction to Skilling.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q2 deceleration is public, but the double-digit full-year claim was never formally withdrawn. Dropping the segment guide hid it rather than retracting it. If it were priced, the Q2 call coverage would have flagged the walk-back, and the summaries found do not.
evidence.independence: Q2 Skilling +2% is from a separate document, the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm). This finding is about the one growth story losing credibility, and is sized small for that reason.

What is not priced is how the Q3 cash balance compares with the roughly $38M pro forma figure: near-breakeven EBITDA plus severance tapering could show cash holding or rising, which would make net cash a larger share of market cap. Financing question answered: this was a repayment from cash, not a raise. No dilution and no going-concern language was found.

evidence.text: Ethos guides far below its outcomes. The Q2 2026 revenue guide of $114-118m (given 2026-05-06) printed at $189.6m, +63% over the midpoint, and the FY2026 guide was raised from $561-565m to $727-731m. Q3 is now guided at $160-164m, which implies a 15% sequential drop from Q2's $189.6m, while sell-side consensus sits at only $163-168m. A print near the Q1/Q2 run-rate (~$190m) would be ~+13% over consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both prior large revenue beats against this company's own guide were bought hard: Q1 2026 (2026-05-06) +32.31%, Q2 2026 (2026-08-03) +21.11% close-to-close (baseline). The first print (2026-02-25), a small beat, moved +3.72%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side consensus ($163-168m) is anchored within a few million of the guide despite two quarters of 60%+ beats. If the market priced the pattern fully, consensus would be near $190m and the stock would not need the beat to hold its 46% post-print run. It is partly priced: the run-up says the buy-side whisper is above consensus.
evidence.independence: Q2 release on EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm) gives Q2 $189.6m and the Q3 guide. Q1 release gives Q1 $193.1m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526208936/life-ex99_1.htm). Benzinga carries the prior FY guide of $561-565m. These sources share the company's own numbers.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide of $727-731m less H1 actuals ($382.7m) and the Q3 midpoint ($162m) implies Q4 of only ~$184m, below the Q1/Q2 run-rate of ~$191m. Any Q3 beat therefore mechanically lifts the FY range, as happened in August (+$166m raise on a $74m Q2 beat).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August FY raise from $561-565m to $727-731m came with the +21.11% reaction. The May release, which carried the first FY guide, moved +32.31%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus that tracks the Q3 guide implies the sell-side also models Q4 near the implied ~$184m. A visible FY raise is the line the stock traded on in August.
evidence.independence: Shares the company-guide document with the first finding, and the raise is largely a mechanical consequence of a Q3 beat, so it is sized down for the overlap. The H1 revenue of $382.7m is from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526335209/life-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: The bar has been raised by the tape. The stock is +18.9% in 20 days, about +46% since the 2026-08-03 print, 2.8% below its 52-week high and +336% off its low. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior LIFE print came into a run-up this large. Into Q2 the stock had not rallied 46% from the previous print.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is the price itself. It is filed because it sets the effective bar: a beat merely to ~$185m against a whisper near $190-200m can be sold. The skew (+5.37) agrees with this direction.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_20d +18.93%, pct_from_52w_high -2.83%. evidence.text: Short interest more than tripled into the print, from 1.26m shares (2026-08-31) to 4.11m (2026-10-15, 2.87 days to cover). That is ~13% of the 31.55m Class A shares, against put/call open interest of only 0.02, so a beat meets a growing short base.

evidence.why_not_priced: FINRA publishes with a lag and the 10-30 settlement is not yet out. A squeeze would show as calls bid and a shrinking short base before the print, and neither is visible. evidence.text: Margins are guided down sharply. Q3 adj. EBITDA guide is $23-25m (~15% margin at the midpoint) against Q2's $35.2m (19%). evidence.text: On 2026-10-19 Evercore ISI (Mark Mahaney) upgraded MTCH from In Line to Outperform and raised the target from $39 to $53, citing app-usage data and its own surveys. These suggest Tinder's recovery is accelerating and could beat management's MAU and payer expectations through 2027. Against that, the Q2 bar is Tinder MAU -7% y/y and payers -5%. Consensus revenue ($891.6M) sits only at the guide midpoint, so street numbers have not moved up with the usage data.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Tinder user trends improved, the stock rose: Q3 2025 (2025-11-04) +5.2% and Q4 2025 (2026-02-03) +5.9%. On Q2 2026 (2026-08-04), DAU improved to -4% but payers fell 5.7% and revenue slightly missed ($853.1M vs $857.8M), and the stock fell 7.49%. Usage gains without payer gains have not been paid for.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock rose about 5% on the upgrade day (Frankfurt +4.9%) and reached $46.67. It has since given back about 9% in a week without a stated cause, which removes much of that move. Consensus revenue and EPS did not rise after the note (revenue drifted down from about $895M). If the usage read were fully priced, the bar would sit at the top of the guide.
evidence.independence: Management's own monthly DAU series points the same way (Q2 letter: July DAU -2.5%, fifth straight monthly improvement, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000891103/000089110326000128/mtch8-k20260804ex992.htm). evidence.text: Management's own Tinder DAU path is Q2 -4% y/y, July -2.5% (fifth straight monthly improvement) and, per the Earnings Whispers preview, August close to flat, with management expecting a positive y/y 'any day now'. On that path Q3 DAU averages about -1% to flat, and a positive September or October month is likely to be disclosed. This would be the first positive y/y DAU in more than three years. The bar is that improvement continues; a first positive month is the upside case.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 DAU at -4% was 'the best in 10 quarters' and the stock still fell 7.49% on payers and revenue. DAU alone has not carried a print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management told the market to expect it, and every preview names DAU turning positive as the test. What is not priced is the size of the turn and whether MAU (-7% in Q2) follows. A clear positive DAU month with MAU narrowing to about -4% would beat the preview framing; DAU near flat with MAU at -6% would read as a stall.
evidence.independence: The August 'close to flat' comes from the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/407957/match-groups-rally-puts-tinders-promised-usage-turn-on-trial-this-quarter), which is AI-assisted and cites management. evidence.text: In the Q2 letter, full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA was guided at or above the high end of the February range ($1.280-1.325B), with margin above 37.5%. FCF was guided to the high end ($1.085-1.135B), SBC lowered to $230-240M, and the Tinder product-test drag cut from $60M to $30-40M. Alternative-payment savings run at about $130M for the year. This sets up a second margin and FCF raise at Q3, while the revenue guide holds near the midpoint as reported.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, adjusted EBITDA rose 14% with a 39% margin and the full-year EBITDA was effectively raised, yet the stock fell 7.49% on the revenue and payer lines. Margin beats have not been paid for on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the company already guided to the high end. The unpriced part is a raise above the high end, given a $10M Q3 Tinder test drag inside a $30-40M full-year envelope and the alternative-payment savings. If priced, consensus EPS would sit above $1.05; the whisper at $1.08 says part of it is.
evidence.independence: Same document as the DAU finding, but a different line (margin and FCF versus usage). The EW preview says FCF is tracking toward the high end and alternative-payment savings are about $130M (https://finviz.com/news/407957/match-groups-rally-puts-tinders-promised-usage-turn-on-trial-this-quarter).

evidence.text: The dollar strengthened after the July 28 rates on which the Q3 and full-year guides rest. evidence.why_not_priced: Analysts often roll FX into Q4 numbers only after the company restates its guide rates. Q4 consensus is not available here, so whether it was cut is unverified. ROKU's value over the window is therefore about $96 + 0.9693 x FOXA, and the stock element is about 39% of the $157 value. Roku's Q3 numbers can only reach the price through deal-break odds.

evidence.why_not_priced: This is not unpriced. It is the frame that says the print is nearly irrelevant. If the market treated this as a normal earnings event, the stock would not sit $1 under deal value with 12% realised vol. The 3.31% straddle comes from an illiquid chain, not from a priced print risk.

evidence.text: The spread to deal value roughly halved on 2026-11-02, before the entry close. Fox also restarted buybacks, though the CFO said not to link them to deal timing. A residual spread of about 0.6-0.8% leaves almost no upside from further tightening. A partial give-back is the more likely small move.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print on the spread. On Nov 2 the spread moved about $1, or 0.6% of ROKU, on Fox's call language alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced at the entry close; the tightening happened intraday on Nov 2. I file it because the residual spread sets the asymmetry for the window: little room up, some room for a give-back if the market rereads 'work cooperatively with the DOJ' as no timeline.
